reviewNotes:
• [Factual information] - Disembarkation timing: the notification gives 4 minutes 8 seconds after the aircraft stopped (07:30:57), which is about 07:35:05. The timeline gives 07:34:40 to 07:38:48, a 4 min 08 s period measured from the airstair, not from the stop. The draft factual section states the timing as "four minutes after it stopped".
  • Draft factual section, take-off roll entry: "five minutes after the end of civil twilight" is not supported by any source. Last light time is not established.
  • Draft factual section, impact entry: "No. 2 propeller was destroyed" overstates the inspection finding, which is three blades beyond limits.
  • Captain's duty start: the crew duty record gives sign-on 06:30 local. The captain's interview background gives 05:10 local.
  • Captain's last simulator check: the crew record gives 11/03/2026. The interview background gives February 2026.
  • First officer's time with the operator: the crew record gives 14 months. The interview background gives 17 months, but a join date of April 2025 is about 14 months at the occurrence date.
  • First sighting range: the first officer's estimate of about 200 m sits uneasily with the reconstruction. Her call came about one second before the reject point at 1,152 m, and the carcasses lay at 1,188 m and 1,221 m.
  • Number of animals struck: the notification records both struck. The captain's safety report records at least one.
  • Both interview records are not finalised. Organisational facts drawn from them (Appendix 8A, training scenarios, briefing on the evening service, sightings) need confirming against the transcripts.
  • [Analysis / External Influences] - AS-139 10.4.3 and the "Documented wildlife plan" evidence: 10.4.3 requires an operator below the threshold to "be able to demonstrate what measures are in place". The evidence states the aerodrome's measures "need not be documented at all" and that it held nothing beyond the Aerodrome Manual 6.3 inspection. Whether the aerodrome could demonstrate its measures as 10.4.3 requires is not addressed, and this bears on the statement that it was not in breach.
  • Timeline item "17/06/2026 21:35:00 Daily movement area inspection": the item is sourced to the aerodrome daily inspection log, but its attached supporting extract is the wildlife sighting log, not the inspection log.
  • [Analysis / Organisational Influences] - Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles: the distance from the animal pad to the first carcass is given three ways. The Evidence field gives 110 m. The photograph note gives 138 m. The Significance field gives "140 m apart" for the pad and both carcasses. The stated positions (1,050 m, 1,188 m and 1,221 m) give 138 m to the first carcass and 171 m to the second. The draft uses the positions only and states no separation.
  • Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles: the investigator notes and test note refer to "the operator's own register". The works register belongs to the aerodrome operator (Tarlton Shire Council), not the aircraft operator. The draft attributes it to the aerodrome operator.
  • Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles: the works register extract is marked as the investigator's description, not a verbatim source, yet it contains quoted register wording. The draft paraphrases that wording. Confirm whether the register entries may be quoted verbatim.
  • [Analysis / Risk Controls] - Rejected take-off training, evidence for influence: states "The captain had two seconds". The CVR shows the first officer's call at 07:30:31 and the reject at 07:30:32, and the captain stated "I never had them". The two seconds appears to be the first officer's sighting window, not the captain's decision time.
  • Rejected take-off training, evidence: both crew stated every scenario "has arrived below V1". TRG-SYL-07 module 4 includes an engine failure at V1 plus 5 kt, continued. The crew statement and the syllabus differ on this point.
  • Timeline entry at 17/06/2026 21:35:00 (daily movement area inspection): the entry cites "Aerodrome daily inspection log, 18/06/2026", but its attached extract is the wildlife sighting log, not the inspection log.
  • [Analysis / Local Conditions] - Fifth sector, 11 hours into duty, 40 minutes behind schedule: the field labelled "Evidence for influence" contains an importance argument (routine exposure on the schedule). The field labelled "Evidence against influence" contains both the "for" and "against" arguments. The drafting followed the content, not the labels.
  • Runway edge lighting intensity reduced the crew's ability to detect the animals: Existence is Inconclusive, yet the causal chains include an edge from this factor to "Take-off rejected 6 kt above V1". That edge asserts a causal path the unresolved test does not support.
  • Runway edge lighting intensity reduced the crew's ability to detect the animals / Timeline 07:30:31: the first officer's estimated range at first sight was about 200 m. The FDR places the sighting call at 07:30:31 and impact at 07:30:33 at a groundspeed of about 111 to 115 kt. The reject point was 1,152 m and the carcasses were at 1,188 m and 1,221 m. Together these suggest a range nearer 100 m at the sighting call. The 200 m figure has been carried as an estimate. The investigator may wish to reconcile it.
  • Take-off commenced with a tailwind above limits: the evidence cites the 06:30, 07:00 and 08:00 UTC observations but omits the 06:00 UTC METAR (08008KT). That observation does not alter the conclusion.
  • [Analysis / Individual Actions] - Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay, Influence note: an estimated further 30 to 40 m beyond the 62 m stopping point gives 92 m to 102 m. That is beyond the end of a 90 m RESA, not "close to the far edge". The arithmetic and the wording need reconciling.
  • Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay, Significance: this credits "the asymmetric braking technique". The FDR extract shows symmetric brake pressure of 2,940 psi and describes no differential braking, so no evidence shown supports an asymmetric technique. The same line refers to "the two seconds", but the margin over the fleet mean was 1.2 seconds. The draft omits both claims.
  • No runway inspection requested before the first departure after last light, Significance: the "20 minutes before the roll" window is not established by any evidence shown for this factor. The draft omits it.
  • Take-off rejected 6 kt above V1, Evidence: the quotation is given as 'Stopping, I have control'. The verbatim CVR transcript reads "Stopping. I have control." The draft quotes the transcript.
  • No runway inspection requested before the first departure after last light: the factor title describes SB512 as the first departure after last light. The evidence shown does not confirm that no other departure followed last light that day.
  • [Analysis / Occurrence Events] - Two kangaroos factor, Evidence: the first officer's estimated range at first sight is around 200 m. At about 113 kt groundspeed, the first officer's own "two seconds. Maybe less" and the carcass positions near 1,188 m suggest a shorter range at 07:30:31. The source of the 200 m estimate is not identified.
  • Two kangaroos factor, Evidence: the eleven sealed-surface log entries are described as "all around last light". The sighting log description states that 38 of the 41 kangaroo entries were around last light. It does not say all eleven sealed-surface entries were.
  • Two kangaroos factor and Strike factor: the carcasses are recorded on the northern half of runway 09. The strike was on the right main gear and No. 2 propeller, which is the southern side on a heading of 09, and the first officer stated that the animals crossed the centreline. This positional discrepancy is not explained.
  • Deceleration factor, Evidence: the 2.6 m/s2 mean is stated as "from maximum braking to the runway end". The FDR readout gives it for 07:30:34 to 07:30:44, while the aircraft left the seal at 07:30:51.
  • Strike factor, Significance: this describes reverse removed "two seconds into a stop". The impact was one second after the reject began (07:30:32 to 07:30:33).
  • No. 2 engine power loss, Evidence: the captain's words are quoted as 'Stopping, I have control'. The verbatim CVR reads "Stopping. I have control."
  • [Conclusions] - "Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles": the distance from the fence pad to the first carcass is recorded as 110 m in the Evidence field and as 138 m in the photograph note and in "Two kangaroos entered the runway strip". The Significance field gives 140 m between the pad and the carcasses. The finding avoids stating a figure.
  • The Conclusions outline placed "Cabin floor proximity emergency lighting partially unserviceable" and "Fifth sector, 11 hours into duty, 40 minutes behind schedule" under the heading "Contributing factors", although both failed Influence. They are placed under Other findings in this draft. The outline also grouped every factor that passed Influence under "Probable cause".
  • The outline omitted the inconclusive matter "Runway edge lighting intensity reduced the crew's ability to detect the animals". It is discussed after the numbered findings, without a finding.
  • "Fifth sector, 11 hours into duty": the field labelled "Evidence against influence" opens with the argument for influence, and the "Evidence for influence" field reads as an importance argument.
  • "Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay": Influence is recorded as very likely, but the outline gave no term. The draft carries very likely.
  • The approved Factual information section marks the following as not established, although the evidence holds them: civil twilight timing, fence condition, the floor lighting functional check result, the edge lighting photometry, and the AS-139 threshold values. It also records two sign-on times (06:30 and 05:10 local).
  • [Recommendations / Documented wildlife plan required only above a size threshold the aerodrome does not meet] - Approved Analysis text, first paragraph: describes "the single daily inspection before the first arrival under Aerodrome Manual 6.3". The evidence for the wildlife plan factor says only "the single pre-first-arrival inspection". The word "daily" is not supported by the evidence shown.
  • Approved Analysis text, final paragraph: the Appendix 8A listing material and the review date of 03/03/2025 sit under the wildlife plan heading. They appear to belong to the factor "Runway inspection required only at listed aerodromes, and the listing criterion is a strike". The paragraph also ends by saying the size threshold "is discussed under External Influences", but it appears inside that discussion.
  • "Cabin floor proximity emergency lighting partially unserviceable" is listed twice, once under Safety issues and once under Other risk factors, with identical tests. It is not finalised in either place.
  • Investigation log, 2026-07-02: refers to an object pending "the fleet ballast answer". No factor in the evidence set corresponds to a ballast question.
  • [Recommendations / Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles] - Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles, Evidence line: the distance from the animal pad at 1,050 m to the first carcass is given as 110 m. The Significance line gives the carcasses at 1,188 m and 1,221 m, which puts the first 138 m from the pad. The Significance line rounds that to 140 m, and the photograph note gives 138 m. The 110 m figure is inconsistent with the recorded positions. The draft gives only the positions and avoids stating a separation.
  • Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles, Safety action: WR-221 describes damage between the 700 m and 1,300 m markers, but the programmed replacement covers 140 m. The record does not establish whether the rest of the WR-221 section is sound or needs work.
  • Safety action status: the replacement was programmed for 09/2026 and is recorded as "In progress" as of 2026-06-25. This collation was generated 2026-10-02, after the programmed month, and no update on completion is recorded.
  • [Recommendations / Evening service approved as a schedule change, route risk assessment not reopened] - Investigation log, 2026-06-19T01:20:00.000Z: the log records that the Head of Flying Operations suspended the evening Tarlton Springs service. No safety action is recorded against this safety issue. The investigator may wish to confirm whether the suspension should be recorded as safety action and assessed as addressing the issue in full or in part.
  • Approved Analysis text for this factor: it states that the evening rotation ran "six days per week". That frequency does not appear in the evidence held for this factor. It may come from the attached extract, which is not reproduced, and should be verified.
  • [Recommendations / Runway inspection required only at listed aerodromes, and the listing criterion is a strike] - Recommendation against "Runway inspection required only at listed aerodromes, and the listing criterion is a strike": its status is Open with a response due 30/09/2026, but the record was generated on 02/10/2026 and shows no response. Please confirm whether a response was received before this section is finalised.
  • The same recommendation also covers a route risk assessment trigger for aerodromes first operated into after last light. That part answers the safety issue "Evening service approved as a schedule change, route risk assessment not reopened" more than this one. Please check it is not repeated or contradicted in that issue's recommendation subsection.
  • [Recommendations / Rejected take-off training covers aircraft system failures below V1 only] - "Rejected take-off training covers aircraft system failures below V1 only": the Importance test is recorded as Not tested. The section specification asks for the issue's safety significance, so that significance has been described from the existence evidence only (five cycles, 214 crew). No Importance confidence is available to support it.
  • "Rejected take-off training covers aircraft system failures below V1 only": no safety action or recommendation is recorded for an issue that passed both Existence and Influence. The subsection therefore states only that none has been recorded.
  • "Rejected take-off training covers aircraft system failures below V1 only": the evidence describes the decision time as "two seconds" with no qualifier. The subsection writes "about two seconds" to avoid implying measured precision. The investigator should confirm whether this figure comes from recorded data or from the captain's account.
  • [Recommendations / Cabin floor proximity emergency lighting partially unserviceable] - Investigation log entry 2026-06-26T04:15:00.000Z states the cabin emergency lighting functional check was "raised off the first officer's account" at the interviews completed that day. However, the functional check on VH-SBQ is dated 24/06/2026, two days earlier. Either the check date, the log entry, or the source of the first officer's observation (an earlier report rather than the interview) needs confirming.
  • The fleet-wide ballast question is unresolved and this issue remains unfinalised. The statement that the fleet's true state is unknown may need revising once that answer is available.
  • [Executive summary] - Executive summary scaffold "Date: 17/06/2026" conflicts with the critical event evidence and the approved Factual information, which give 18/06/2026 UTC. The draft uses 18/06/2026.
  • Perimeter fence object: the evidence gives the pad at 1,050 m as "110 m before the point at which the first carcass was recovered". The carcass is at 1,188 m, which gives 138 m, and the kangaroo object and photograph rationale both say 138 m. The fence significance line gives "140 m apart".
  • Scaffold Safety issues list tags the cabin floor proximity lighting "(unlikely)". That is its Influence term. Its Importance term is very likely, and the draft uses very likely.
  • The approved Factual information marks three items as not established that the evidence does hold: the time of last light and civil twilight, the fence condition, and the floor lighting functional check result. These may need reconciling with the evidence.
  • Approved Conclusions finding 10 (strike) carries no likelihood term, although its tests are recorded as virtually certain.
